label: August 1910
atlas_dek: The episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1910 from our dossiers, placed on 1910 county lines and by month (some July events were first reported in August). Hover for a short summary; select a dot to read the account in the sidebar. Drafts: no entry has had human review.
reader_intro:
Dossiers for 69 episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1910. They come from the 112 located events in the August 1910 table, which includes July events first reported in August, among them the Slocum massacre in Anderson County, Texas, and one event found while writing the dossiers. We did not write dossiers for 31 events that were plainly out of scope from the table alone (no one harmed, a white victim, no race given, earlier years recalled in editorials) or that repeat another record, and seven more belong to other months of 1910. Searches covered August papers, plus September papers for more on known episodes.

Twelve of the 81 dossiers are set aside. Three are duplicates folded into another record: a garbled editorial echo of the Slocum massacre, the killing of Will Burley at Priscilla, one of the Slocum dead, and a second report of the mob attack on the Looker building at Moline, Illinois. A police killing at Ridgeway, Virginia, happened in June and is held for its month. Eight are out of scope. The lynching reported near Nottingham, Alabama, was found by a coroner’s jury to be a suicide; the Beck–Tolnay inventory lists it as a lynching. No report gives anyone’s race for the “race riot” at Gray, Georgia, which fuller reports describe as a feud between two families, or for the lynching threat against the Alexander brothers at Kenton, Tennessee. The brawl at a coal operation near Ashland, West Virginia, and the fight on a Southampton County excursion train were two-sided, with the injured on the white side. At Fernwood, Pennsylvania, the crowd was Black and chased the white man who had shot a Black man, and the threat against George Chivers in Chicago came from Black neighbors angry at an informer. The posse search at Elizabeth City, North Carolina, harmed and threatened no one.

Police violence is kept generously: men shot while fleeing, resisting arrest, or escaping a convict gang, and shots that missed, are all included. Only gunfights over a crime in progress are set aside. Where an inventory lists a lynching that the papers describe differently, as with Tom Weaver, killed by a posse near Seville, Georgia, the entry keeps the inventory match and states the difference. Where no report gives the victim’s race, the entry says so.

Method: a research agent (Sonnet) searched Black and white papers. A write-up agent (Opus) wrote the dossier with keyed citations, and a code check confirmed every quote and citation against the article text. Black-press clippings are shown as page images; white-press clippings are page images where we could place them on the scan, otherwise text.

Drafts: no entry has had human review.
